newsitem.title: INDIA: India Left vows no change in coalition leader.
newsitem.headline: India Left vows no change in coalition leader.

text.p: India's Left Front, a key constituent of the defeated United Front, said on Wednesday it was opposed to replacing caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda unless the Congress party withdrew its claim to power.

"We are not prepared to give them a veto on that," Harkishen Singh Surjeet, general secretary of the Communist Party of India (Marxist), (CPI-M), told reporters. "Do (the Congress) they want to determine the choice of the leader? This cannot happen."

The Congress party, which last week triggered the fall of Deve Gowda's government by withdrawing its crucial make-or-break support, had staked its claim to form a new government in a letter to President Shankar Dayal Sharma last month.
On Monday, Congress said it would support a new United Front government, provided the alliance named a new leader. But it has not officially withdrawn its claim.
Earlier on Wednesday, a senior United Front leader said there was a "distinct possibility" a new government would be forged under its leadership in the next few days.
President Shankar Dayal Sharma has called a special session of parliament between April 21 and 23 to allow discussion and a possible vote on the 1997/98 (April-March) budget.
